messages.author: c0678c94baffe75f
messages.subject: problem of line proportionality
parts:
Hi,

I have a problem of proportionality with geom_line() and geom_segment(). I wrote a function with geom_segment so that the line size (width) would be proportional to a continuous variable. I exported the plot in .svg and realized that the line width in the legend wasn't proportional.

You can reproduce it with this example (taken from the online documentation of geom_line). Export the last plot in .svg and compare line width: the thicker line (value = 10) is smaller than 4 times the thiner line (2.5). 

mry <- do.call(rbind, by(movies, round(movies$rating), function(df) {
  nums <- tapply(df$length, df$year, length)
  data.frame(rating=round(df$rating[1]), year = as.numeric(names(nums)), number=as.vector(nums))
}))
p <- ggplot(mry, aes(x=year, y=number, group=rating))
p + geom_line(aes(size = rating))

Does anyone have an explanation and a solution?

Thanks

--
Hadrien

messages.author: c0678c94baffe75f
messages.subject: Re: problem of line proportionality
parts:
I'm sorry but I have to insist with my proportionality problem. With geom_line() or geom_segment() (see example before), I sometimes get a better proportionality adding scale_size(), but it's not accurate and I can't understand why. I mean, when I set a colour I get exactly that colour, when I set a position I get exactly that position, but when I set a proportion I just get nearly (if lucky) that proportion.

Please try this, there is a factor 2 difference in the value, but a factor 6 difference in the proportion :

xori <- c(1, 2)
xend <- c(2, 3)
yori <- c(2, 4)
yend <- c(1, 2)
val <- c(10, 20)
df <- data.frame(xori, xend, yori, yend, val)

ggplot(df) + geom_segment(aes(x = xori, y = yori, xend = xend, yend = yend, size = val))

Please help !

--
Hadrien

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: problem of line proportionality
parts:
Hi Hadri,

See ?scale_size and you will see that the default is range=c(1,6). If you want a different range just say so like this:

ggplot(df) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = xori, y = yori, xend = xend, yend = yend, size = val)) +
    scale_size_continuous(range=c(1, 2))

Best,
Ista
